description.value: A retrospective study evaluated SVM classifiers trained on 3D T1 MRI for differential diagnosis of EOAD, LOAD, FTD and depression, and assessed whether SVM weight maps improved radiologists' diagnostic performance.

spans.text: We studied 34 patients with early-onset Alzheimer's disease (EOAD), 49 with late-onset AD (LOAD), 39 with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and 24 with depression from the pre-existing cohort CLIN-AD.

description.value: Retrospective study of patients from the pre-existing CLIN-AD cohort, with diagnostic classification using routine clinical MRI and blinded radiological readings performed without and with SVM weight maps.

Classifiers were created using Support vector machine (SVM) for each pair of diagnostic groups (LOAD vs. depression, LOAD vs. FTD, EOAD vs. depression and EOAD vs. FTD).
Classification performances were assessed using the balanced accuracy defined as: (sensitivity + specificity)/2.

10-fold cross validations (CV) were performed to evaluate the performance of the classifiers with another nested 10-fold CV for unbiased search of the optimal value of the regularization hyperparameter.

value: The use of weight maps did not significantly improve diagnostic performance for LOAD versus depression.
The classifier was not reported as significantly more accurate than the radiologists for this diagnostic pair.

spans.text: Across the four radiologists, the use of weight maps significantly improved the diagnostic performances for FTD vs. EOAD (P < 0.001) but not for other diagnostic pairs.
